title: Maize (Corn) — Overview for East Africa
content:
## Maize (Zea mays)

Maize is the most important staple crop in East Africa, grown by over 90% of smallholder farmers in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda.

### Recommended Varieties for East Africa

**Highland (above 1500m):** H614D, H6213, DK8031, Pioneer PH4 — good for Rift Valley, Nyeri, Meru, Kilimanjaro highlands.

**Mid-altitude (1000–1500m):** H513, DK8031, Seedco SC403 — Nakuru, Eldoret, Arusha, Kampala surrounds.

**Lowland (below 1000m):** Katumani Composite, DH04, KSTP94 — Coast, Turkana, low-lying areas. These are drought-tolerant varieties.

**Disease-resistant options:** DK777, Afya (MLN-tolerant), WS403 (MLN-tolerant) — critical in MLN-affected zones.

### Key Agronomic Details

- **Planting density:** 53,000–67,000 plants/ha (75cm × 25cm, one plant per hole)
- **Seed rate:** 25–30 kg/ha
- **Planting depth:** 5cm
- **Germination:** 5–7 days
- **Days to 50% silking:** 55–65 days (highland varieties take longer)
- **Days to maturity:** 90–120 days depending on altitude and variety

### Fertilizer Requirements

- **Planting (DAP or NPK 23:23:0):** 50 kg/ha placed 5cm beside the seed at planting
- **Topdressing (CAN or Urea):** Apply at V4–V6 stage (4–6 leaves), 50 kg CAN/ha
- **Second topdressing (optional):** At knee-height if rains are good, another 25 kg CAN/ha

### Weed Management

Critical window: first 6 weeks after germination. Hand weed at 3 weeks and 6 weeks. Herbicide option: Atrazine (pre-emergence) + Nicosulfuron (post-emergence at V3–V5).
content_sw:
## Mahindi (Zea mays)

Mahindi ni zao muhimu zaidi la chakula Afrika Mashariki, inayolimwa na zaidi ya 90% ya wakulima wadogo Kenya, Tanzania, na Uganda.

### Aina Zinazopendekezwa Afrika Mashariki

**Maeneo ya juu (zaidi ya 1500m):** H614D, H6213, DK8031 — nzuri kwa Bonde la Ufa, Nyeri, Kilimanjaro.

**Maeneo ya kati (1000–1500m):** H513, DK8031, Seedco SC403 — Nakuru, Eldoret, Arusha.

**Maeneo ya chini (chini ya 1000m):** Katumani Composite, DH04 — Pwani, maeneo ya joto. Hizi ni aina zinazostahimili ukame.

### Matumizi ya Mbolea

- **Upanzi (DAP au NPK):** Kilo 50/hekta karibu na mbegu wakati wa kupanda
- **Ziada (CAN au Urea):** Weka wakati mahindi yana majani 4–6, kilo 50 CAN/hekta

title: Maize Nutrient Deficiency — Diagnosis Guide
content:
## Maize Nutrient Deficiency — How to Diagnose

### Nitrogen Deficiency (most common)

**Symptoms:** Yellowing starts at the tip of lower (older) leaves and moves down the leaf midrib in a V-shape. Progresses up the plant over time. Plants appear pale green to yellow overall.

**Cause:** Insufficient nitrogen in soil, excessive rainfall leaching, or delayed topdressing.

**Treatment:**
- Apply CAN (Calcium Ammonium Nitrate) at 50 kg/ha immediately
- Or Urea at 25–30 kg/ha (band placement near plants, cover with soil)
- Best time: when plants are knee-high and growing actively
- Emergency: foliar spray of 2% Urea solution (20g urea in 1 litre water) on leaves

### Potassium Deficiency

**Symptoms:** Brown scorching on leaf edges and tips, starting with lower leaves. Leaf margins look 'burned'. Stalks may be weak.

**Treatment:** Apply Muriate of Potash (MOP) at 50 kg/ha.

### Phosphorus Deficiency

**Symptoms:** Purple or reddish-purple coloration on lower leaves and leaf undersides, especially in young plants. Stunted growth.

**Treatment:** Apply DAP or TSP at 50 kg/ha at planting for next season. Foliar: apply mono-potassium phosphate (MKP) as foliar spray.

### Zinc Deficiency

**Symptoms:** White or yellow striping on young leaves, especially in the middle of the leaf. Interveinal chlorosis.

**Treatment:** Apply zinc sulfate at 10 kg/ha or foliar spray with zinc sulfate (2g/L).

### Important Note on MLN vs Nitrogen Deficiency

Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN) can look like nitrogen deficiency but is **much more serious**. Key differences:
- MLN shows mottled/mosaic patterns and progresses faster
- MLN causes premature cob drying and empty cobs
- MLN is caused by virus (spread by thrips/aphids) — no chemical cure
- Nitrogen deficiency responds to CAN/Urea within 2 weeks — MLN does not
content_sw:
## Upungufu wa Virutubisho kwa Mahindi

### Upungufu wa Nitrojeni (kawaida zaidi)

**Dalili:** Majani ya chini yanageuka njano kuanzia ncha hadi katikati. Mmea mzima unaonekana manjano.

**Tiba:**
- Weka CAN kilo 50/hekta haraka
- Au Urea kilo 25–30/hekta karibu na mmea, funika na udongo
- Dawa ya majani: Urea 2% (gramu 20 katika lita 1 ya maji)

### Upungufu wa Potasiamu

**Dalili:** Kingo za majani zinaungua hudhurungi, kuanzia majani ya chini.

### Upungufu wa Fosforasi

**Dalili:** Rangi ya zambarau kwenye majani ya chini na upande wa chini wa majani, haswa kwa miche michanga.

title: Tomato Farming — East Africa Guide
content:
## Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum)

### Recommended Varieties for East Africa

**Hybrid varieties (commercial, high yield):**
- **Anna F1** — very popular in Tanzania and Kenya; tolerant to bacterial wilt and TYLCV; 90–100 days to maturity; yield 40–60 t/ha
- **Kilele F1** — medium-large fruits; good shelf life; widely used in Kenya highlands
- **Tylka F1** — specifically bred for TYLCV resistance; good for hot lowland areas
- **Cal J** — determinate, good for processing; popular in large-scale farming

**Open-pollinated varieties (OPV, cheaper seed):**
- **Roma VF** — paste tomato; determinate; drought-tolerant
- **Mstari** — popular in Tanzania; heat-tolerant

### Nursery and Transplanting

1. Prepare nursery beds with 1:1 soil:compost mix
2. Sow seeds thinly, cover lightly with compost
3. Germination: 5–8 days
4. Transplant at 3–4 weeks (15–20 cm height, 3–4 true leaves)
5. Transplant spacing: 60cm × 60cm (determinate) or 100cm × 60cm (indeterminate/staked)
6. Transplant in evening or on cloudy day; water immediately

### Fertilizer Schedule

- **Basal (at transplanting):** 5–10g DAP per hole
- **Week 3–4:** CAN 50 kg/ha + foliar compound fertilizer
- **Flowering (week 6–7):** Stop N-heavy fertilizer; use P/K-heavy fertilizer (e.g. 0-0-60)
- **Fruiting:** Calcium-Magnesium foliar to prevent BER (blossom-end rot)

### Expected Yield and Market Prices

- **Good crop (with irrigation):** 30–50 t/ha
- **Rain-fed, good season:** 15–25 t/ha
- **Market price (Tanzania, 2024–2025):** TZS 300–800/kg ex-farm (USD 0.12–0.32/kg)
- **Market price (Kenya, 2024–2025):** KES 30–80/kg ex-farm depending on season
- **High-value periods:** May–July (between rains) and November–January

### Irrigation Requirements

- Needs consistent moisture — avoid drought stress at flowering/fruiting
- Drip irrigation preferred (reduces leaf wetness, lower disease pressure)
- Flood/furrow irrigation: water every 3–5 days in dry season
- Total water requirement: 400–600mm per season
content_sw:
## Nyanya (Solanum lycopersicum)

### Aina Zinazopendekezwa Afrika Mashariki

**Chotara (mavuno mengi):**
- **Anna F1** — maarufu sana Tanzania na Kenya; inastahimili kuoza kwa bakteria na TYLCV; mavuno tani 40–60/hekta
- **Kilele F1** — matunda makubwa ya kati; nzuri kwa miinuko ya Kenya

### Bei za Soko

- **Tanzania:** TZS 300–800/kg
- **Kenya:** KES 30–80/kg
- **Wakati mzuri:** Mei–Julai na Novemba–Januari
